extracted.intended_audience: journalism educators and university facilities planners (especially at smaller institutions)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for designing, equipping, and budgeting teaching facilities (newsroom, graphics lab, editing/film benches) for journalism, broadcasting, and related communications programs at a university. Emphasis on economical, expandable solutions appropriate to smaller institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual program requirements determine facility planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Of course, the most important considerations in the planning of physical facilities are the individual program requirements of the institution in question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design facilities to meet the specific program's course requirements, enrollment projections, and institutional context (e.g., small liberal arts college vs. major university). Tailor capacity and equipment to projected course load (example: average journalism major needs ~3 newswriting courses, 1 editing, 1 graphic design, 1 advertising copywriting/design).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide facilities for immediate use with capacity for future growth
rubrics_metrics.description: The planning recognizes that the problems of the new technology can be faced within a budget by providing facilities for immediate use with the capacity for future growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize equipment and wiring that allow later upgrade (e.g., wiring desks for future video display terminals, leaving space for OCR/photo-typesetter additions). Choose scalable layouts and infrastructure rather than fully outfitting with expensive future tech up front.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design multipurpose newsroom for print and broadcast
rubrics_metrics.description: The newsroom was designed to be used for both the print and broadcast programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where enrollment and space are limited, create flexible newsroom layouts that serve multiple disciplines (print, broadcast, editing) to maximize utility and cross-training opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity and seating planning (size for present and near-term growth)
rubrics_metrics.description: Space for 12 students provides an ideal number for teaching newswriting and will sustain the number of students anticipated for the next two years. Five more typing stations can be provided by moving the film editing equipment to a new location.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan workstations to accommodate current class sizes but allow modest expansion via reconfiguration. Example: provide 12-student capacity with options to add more stations when equipment or space is relocated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose industry-standard equipment to match employer expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: The five IBM Selectric II units were chosen for two reasons. First, they are the typewriters used by all major newspapers...Second, plans for the third year of the program call for the addition of an optical character reader and an automatic photo typesetter...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select equipment (e.g., IBM Selectric II) that students will encounter in the workplace; this improves student employability and allows compatibility with industry workflows (OCR, scanning).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide wiring and IT attachment points for future computer integration
rubrics_metrics.description: This unit is wired for the addition of three video display terminals which will connect with the university's IBM 370 computer. Late in 1974 or early in 1975 grant money should be available for an IBM Advanced Text Management System...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if immediate computer terminals are not purchased, wire desks and plan infrastructure to support terminals and text-management systems when funding arrives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate and budget for electrical upgrades and HVAC in older buildings
rubrics_metrics.description: Because of problems encountered in the old building the original newsroom budget of $8500 fell $450 short. Additional electrical wiring to provide for future equipment expansion cost $500. It was also necessary to provide air conditioning to make the facilities usable year-round.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect existing building systems early; budget for rewiring, additional circuits, and air conditioning especially when repurposing older rooms for equipment-heavy labs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer durable, higher-quality equipment over 'economy' models for student use
rubrics_metrics.description: Experience at other institutions had shown that it did not pay to use 'economy' models of equipment which did not stand up to the rugged use of students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in robust paste-up and lab equipment that will withstand heavy student use even if initial cost is higher; this reduces replacement/repair costs and downtime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus instruction on current industry practices (e.g., cold-type paste-up)
rubrics_metrics.description: Since virtually all newspapers have now adopted the cold-type paste-up system of operation, no consideration was given to teaching the actual mechanics of letterpress preparation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach technologies and workflows that reflect contemporary industry practice rather than outdated mechanics; equip labs accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule shared spaces carefully when facilities are multi-use
rubrics_metrics.description: The graphics laboratory found itself in the unlikely situation of temporarily sharing facilities with a radio studio. The only real problem that this presented was one of space. Careful scheduling prevents most conflicts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When labs are shared across disciplines, implement careful scheduling and identify priorities to minimize conflicts until dedicated space is available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include operating supplies in initial budget planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Because of the addition of operating supplies (including tape machines, scissors, border tapes, etc.) which might normally be included in a yearly operating budget, the original graphics lab budget of $5300 fell $150 short.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for consumables and small tools when estimating costs; otherwise equipment-only budgets will be insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use equipment that gives varied, hands-on student experience cost-effectively
rubrics_metrics.description: The setting of headlines has proven in the past to provide valuable experience for students to become familiar with the uses of type. ... budgetary considerations dictated the purchase of a relatively inexpensive Stripprinter. The main virtue of this machine is that type fonts cost only $6.00 so that a great variety of type can be made available to the students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select some lower-cost devices that still provide pedagogical value (e.g., stripprinter with cheap fonts) so students can practice a range of tasks affordably.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide appropriate furniture and ergonomic heights
rubrics_metrics.description: Typing surfaces 2€'6€" high. Desk surfaces 30" high. all plastic tops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify desk and typing surface heights and durable tops suitable for typing/paste-up work; ensure furniture supports intensive student use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design editing desks and work areas to accommodate required roles and equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: An editing desk was designed for five reporters plus the editor's slot. This unit is wired for the addition of three video display terminals...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Customize desks to the pedagogical workflow (reporter slots, editor slot, wiring for terminals) so classroom practice mirrors newsroom roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide sufficient light and layout surfaces for graphics work
rubrics_metrics.description: Approximately 12 students can use the work area comfortably...There are two 46" x 32" light tables, two 46" x 32" paste-up tables, and a 12' flat work table built over the low storage cabinets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equip graphics labs with enough light tables, paste-up tables, and large flat work surfaces to accommodate the student cohort; provide storage under work surfaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan for relocation of specialized equipment to free up general-purpose workstations
rubrics_metrics.description: Five more typing stations can be provided by moving the film editing equipment to a new location.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize spatial allocation so specialized equipment can be moved to expand general-use capacity as program needs change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track costs carefully and expect modest overruns for physical work
rubrics_metrics.description: The original newsroom budget of $8500 fell $450 short. Additional electrical wiring...cost $500. Carpet and ceiling installation, electrical, air conditioning accounted for notable physical costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include contingency for physical work (carpet, ceiling, wiring, HVAC) and be prepared for modest budget increases when retrofitting older spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim for economical solutions appropriate to smaller institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: While these plans might have limited use at a major university which measures students by the hundred rather than by the score, they are workable and economical for smaller institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt cost-effective, modestly scaled designs (e.g., 12–15 student capacities) that prioritize functionality and expandability over full-scale industrial outfitting.
